Repository: pytorch/vision ITEM #9687 Type: issue State: open Title: Use a safe extraction filter for dataset tar archives Author: user-1 Created: 2026-09-29 Labels: (none) Body: > **AI-assisted issue conversion (Codex).** Original report and reproduction by @user-3; all credit belongs to the original reporter. > > Source: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/security/advisories/GHSA-m4rq-h4j7-8887 > > The reporter identifies `_extract_tar()` calling `tar.extractall(to_path)` without an explicit extraction filter. On Python environments whose default permits fully trusted extraction, crafted member paths can write outside the destination. Suggested hardening: explicitly use `filter="data"`, accounting for supported Python versions. The original report below contains truncated text and an incomplete reproduction; it is preserved as submitted. > > This conversion has not independently reproduced or verified the report.
Original report by @user-3 (verbatim) > ### Summary > `torchvision.datasets.utils.extract_archive()` (and its caller `download_and_extract_archive()`) extract `.tar`/`.tgz`/`.tbz` archives by calling `tarfile.extractall()` **without a member filter**. On Python 3.10–3.13 the `tarfile` default is `filter="fully_trusted"`, so a tar member whose name contains `..` (or an absolute path) is written **outside** the caller-specified destination directory. An application that extracts an attacker-influenced archive through this public API can have arbitrary files created/overwritten outside the target directory (e.g. `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, a `.py` on `sys.path`, cron/config files), which can escalate to remote code execution. > > ### Details > Vulnerable sink — `torchvision/datasets/utils.py`, `_extract_tar()`: > > ```python > def _extract_tar(from_path, to_path, compression): > with tarfile.open(from_path, f"r:{compression[1:]}" if compression else "r") as tar: > tar.extractall(to_path) # no filter= -> unsafe on Python <= 3.13 > ``` > > Reached from the documented public API: > > - `extract_archive(from_path, to_path=None, ...)` → `_ARCHIVE_EXTRACTORS[".tar"] == _extract_tar` → `tar.extractall(to_path)` > - `download_and_extract_archive(url, download_root, extract_root=None, ...)` → downloads `url`, then `extract_archive(archive, extract_root)` > > Because no member filter is applied, `tarfile` on Python 3.10–3.13 follows `..` components and absolute paths in member names and writes them relative to the process, not confined to `to_path`. (The sibling `_extract_zip` path relies on `zipfile.extractall`, which CPython path-sanitizes; the tar path is the issue.) > > This is the classic unsafe-`tarfile.extractall` weakness (CVE-2007-4559 family). > > ### PoC > `_extract_tar` copied verbatim and driven with a malicious tar (one member named `../pwned_OUTSIDE_target.txt`): > > ```python > import os, io, tarfile, tempfile > > def _extract_tar(from_path, to_path, compression): # verbatim from torchvision > with tarfile.open(from_path, f"r:{compression[1:]}" if compression else "r") as tar: > tar.extractall(to_path) > > work = tempfile.mkdtemp(); target = os.path.join(work, "extract_here"); os.makedirs(target) > tarp = os.path.join(work, "malicious.tar") > with tarfile.open(tarp, "w") as t: > data = b"owned\n"; ti = tarfile.TarInfo("../pwned_OUTSIDE_target.txt"); ti.size = len > t.addfile(ti, io.BytesIO(data)) > > _extract_tar(tarp, target, None) > print("written outside target:", os.path.exists(os.path.join(work, "pwned_OUTSIDE_target. > ``` > > - On Python 3.10–3.13: prints `written outside target: True` — the file escapes `target`. > - On Python 3.14+: PEP 706 makes `filter="data"` the default, so extraction is refused (`untime-mitigated. > > A real attacker uses a member name such as `../../../../home//.ssh/authorized_keys` > > ### Impact > Directory traversal / arbitrary file write (CWE-22). Affects any application that passes e or URL to `extract_archive()` / `download_and_extract_archive()` while running on Python 3.10–3.13 (e.g. services that accept user-supplied dataset bundles or community model/chen's own dataset flows use hardcoded, integrity-checked mirrors and are notattacker-controlled by default. Arbitrary file write can lead to remote code execution. > > ### Suggested fix > Pass the hardening filter explicitly (available on Python 3.10+, also silences the 3.12/3 > > ```python > def _extract_tar(from_path, to_path, compression): > with tarfile.open(from_path, f"r:{compression[1:]}" if compression else "r") as tar: > tar.extractall(to_path, filter="data") > ```
